safety_boundaries: Uses checked-in fixtures and generated local examples only.
Does not read live market data, private context, workflow files, environment variables, or command history.
Does not place trades, contact brokers, determine suitability, or recommend buying, selling, or holding any product.
Treats position sizing and guardrail outputs as educational review aids, not instructions.

cold_user_question: If the underlying ends close to flat after a choppy path, why can a 3x daily-reset product still lag a simple 3x multiple?
guardrails: Limit holding period assumptions when daily swings dominate the thesis.
Run compare-runs before replacing one leveraged product or path with another.
Record path-decay tolerance in the pretrade plan before sizing the position.
not_investment_advice: This scenario pack is for scenario planning and education only. It is not investment advice, a recommendation, or a suitability determination.
plain_english_answer: The example decomposes the modeled ending NAV against the simple multiple. The path-decay field shows the multi-day compounding gap created by alternating daily returns and fee drag.
takeaways: Compare ending ETP return with the simple multiple before treating leverage as a linear multi-day exposure.
A choppy path can make the daily reset product worse than the simple multiple even when the underlying move looks modest.
The gap is expressed in NAV points so a new user can inspect it without live prices.
